of: A mechanism by which a previously available course of action becomes unexercisable without its holder declining it and without any party at the holder's own table deciding about it, named with the condition lost (a permission, a capability, a counterparty, a coordination), the carrier that runs the clock, and the last intervention that could have kept it, and sorted by what the clock is made of, from clocks the holder never started to clocks the holder's own care for the option started: a closure that must strike before it can be known, a date on someone else's docket, a date on the option's parent, the holder's own development, the record's last witness, the world healing faster than the forum, a ratifier's term, a counterparty's transfer or planning cycle, a coordination's half-life, the holder's own growth, then the act that vests, the exercise that keeps, the readiness that spoils, the move on a neighbouring matter, the new state's first act, the machine that holds the option open, and the pause paper whose renewal belongs to the adversary.
map_register: Operator-grade and concrete: bank holidays and Sunday decrees, bar dates and opt-out postcards, emergency authorizations, eye patches, last-known-well times, mootness and class certification, adjournment sine die, memoranda of lease, reorganizations that absorb a vacancy, sixty-day signatures, approval ceilings, poured footings, empty flights and irrigated fields, thawed vials, first responsive pleadings, first writes, ECMO circuits and mine pumps, tolling agreements; drawn from capital controls, bankruptcy, public-health law, paediatrics, stroke care, constitutional litigation, legislatures, real property, employment, recall elections, mergers, land use, aviation and water law, cold-chain logistics, patent and civil procedure, software migration, transplant medicine, and litigation practice.

items.out: Weekend closure: you want your money out, and you want it now, and the door is shut for exactly that reason. The authority that closes the exit cannot say so beforehand, because saying so is the starting gun for everyone who wants what you want, so the shutting is done in the hours when wanting is useless: the Friday night, the bank holiday, the Sunday address. The Greek banks that did not open on Monday 29 June 2015 after a Sunday speech; the Cypriot bank holiday of March 2013, stretched, after parliament refused the first levy, until the bail-in was law; the Argentine corralito announced on a Saturday in December 2001; the export licence suspended, the delisting published after the fact. What is taken from you is a permission, the leave to move what is yours. The clock is the authority's calendar, aligned to the hours you are locked out. The one bite that could have fed you was a transfer made on rumour, with the whole price of appetite attached, the chance of being wrong and the discount the rumour market charges; the deposits that left Greece that spring left on nothing better. So the tell: this is the one expiry on the map whose notice cannot come before it, and a holder who waits for a date is waiting for a thing the mechanism forbids to exist. Wanting it more does nothing; wanting it earlier is the whole game. It adds to runway-illusions' Cash behind glass, which counts the deposit taken into receivership on a Friday as owned and unreachable, the mechanism that chose the Friday. It is not investor-tells' Let it lapse, a fuse the founder can probe by letting it pass, since a closure that can be probed need not be a surprise; and not a withdrawn offer or a rival's foreclosure, which someone at your own table decides, since the decree is an authority's rule on a class and nobody at your table decided about you. The item stands on that fence and not on any claim that the exit dies as a side effect: the decree forbids the exit by name.

Bar date in the newspaper: you want to be paid, and you want to keep the right to sue on your own, and the date on which that goes unfed was fixed in a room you were not in, in a proceeding you are deemed to have read. The bankruptcy court's bar date for proofs of claim, noticed to creditors the debtor could not name by a notice in a newspaper; the class settlement whose opt-out date arrives on a postcard that looks like advertising; the probate creditor's window that opens and shuts after the notice runs in the county paper. What is taken is a permission, the standing to be paid or to sue on one's own. The clock is the bar-date order together with the rule of constructive notice, under which publication counts as your knowledge precisely because nobody could name you. The one bite that would have kept the plate is a one-page proof of claim or a signed opt-out, the cheapest filing in the law and the least often made, because the person who would make it is by construction the one who was not told. Appetite is no defence here; you would have had to want it enough to read the legal notices. It adds to runway-illusions' Stamp's clock, a permission with a date you can read on the stamp: here the date is written on someone else's docket and imputed to you. It is not deal-deaths' Missing witness, since nothing is missing from the record, only you from the room.

Emergency over: you want to keep using a permission that was carved out of a bigger paper, and the bigger paper has a term of its own, so your grant dies when its parent does, whatever its merits, with no date printed on it. The emergency-use authorization that ends when the declaration it was issued under is terminated, which is a different paper from the public-health emergency that ended in May 2023 and left the authorizations standing; the cross-state telehealth licence that lapsed with each state's emergency in 2021 and 2022; the wartime power; the pilot programme run under a waiver; the sub-lease that dies with the head lease. What is taken is a permission. The clock is the parent instrument's date, which you never signed and may never have read, since the grant you did read carried no date; before anything else you have to find which parent paper carries it. The move that would have kept it is conversion, a full approval, a permanent rule, a licence in your own name, filed while the parent still stands, and conversion is slow enough that it must be started while the emergency looks endless, which is exactly when nobody wants to start it. The appetite that saves you here is for the permanent, and it has to be acted on while the temporary is still feeding you. It is not Bar date in the newspaper, where the date is on a docket and imputed, since here the date is on a different paper than the option and is honest; and not lead-time-floors' Calendar with nothing in it, a wait the rule imposes, since here the rule does not wait but ends.

Patch before seven: the child wants nothing; the child does not know there is an eye to save. The appetite has to live in someone else, because the clock lives in the body and runs on a schedule the holder cannot know, so the last intervention is necessarily in another hand. Amblyopia is most correctable by patching the good eye in the first years and responds less, and less completely, after about seven, though the trials of the 2000s found response into the early teens; the clubfoot cast in infancy; the second language spoken without an accent, which is contested as a hard window; the duckling that imprints in its first day. What is taken is a capability, the cortex's willingness to rewire. The clock is the developmental timetable, and the holder is a child who does not know there is an eye to save. The move that would have kept it is a screening, the preschool vision check, the parent who notices a squint, so the option belongs to one person and its keeping to another, and where no screening programme exists the option expires unseen at a rate that is a property of the programme and not of the child. This is the item where the wanting must be done on someone else's behalf: the want that saves the eye is the parent's and the programme's, never the child's. It adds to Last known well, where a witness dates the option, the case in which the holder cannot be its own witness at all. It is not a use-it-or-lose-it, since nothing the child does or leaves undone runs the clock.

Last known well: the artery might still allow it. The body might still take the drug. You are refused not because the tissue says no but because nobody saw when it started; the option is dated by the last witness to the fact rather than by the fact, so it expires when the proof runs out while the body might still allow it. The stroke patient who wakes with the deficit is ineligible for thrombolysis because the four-and-a-half-hour window is counted from when she was last seen well, which was bedtime, so the wake-up stroke lost the drug regardless of when the artery closed; the same rule dates the opened vial with no time written on the label and the sample whose chain of custody has a gap, each treated as expired at the earliest time it could have been. What is taken is a capability, a treatment the protocol now forbids. The clock is the protocol's timestamp rule, which asks for a witness and not for the tissue. The move that would have kept it is a witness: someone awake, a time written on the vial, or a witness of a different kind, the imaging that reads the tissue's own clock, by which the WAKE-UP trial of 2018 returned the drug to patients with no witnessed onset. What you want is still physically on the table and is denied on a proof, so the wanting has to go at the proof and not at the body. It adds to witness-architectures, which asks what must exist for a trace to form, the option that dies for want of a trace while the fact would still allow it. It is not Patch before seven, where the body's own clock has run, since here the body's clock may not have run and the record's has.

Mooted: you wanted a ruling, and the harm ended before the forum reached it, so nobody had to say no and nobody ruled; the situation resolved itself faster than the body that would decide it moves. The student whose challenge to a law school's admissions was dismissed as moot because he was about to graduate (DeFunis, 1974); the pregnancy over before the appeal; the election held before the ballot-access case; the tenant evicted before the housing court sits; the employee whose grievance is mooted by the reorganization that abolished the post. What is taken is a permission, the justiciability of the claim. The clock is the ratio of the forum's pace to the harm's duration, a number nobody at your table sets. The move that would have kept it is a structure that outlives the individual harm: the class certified before the named plaintiff's harm ends, which is what Sosna (1975) allowed, or the doctrine that a harm capable of repetition yet evading review may be decided anyway, which is what Roe rested on. So the option is kept by a coordination or by a rule and never by hurrying; the appetite for a ruling has to be built bigger than one plaintiff, or it is over the day the plaintiff's harm is. It is not deal-deaths' Cost of the last mile, where the surplus is eaten on a curve, since here nothing is eaten and the harm is simply over; and not Bar date in the newspaper, since there is no date anywhere.

Session ends: the body that could have said yes runs out of its own term with your matter still pending, and its successor never has to say no. The bills that die on adjournment sine die and must be reintroduced from the beginning; the treaty signed and waiting on a parliament that is dissolved; the permit application before a council that is re-elected; the approval the old board agreed in the hallway and had not yet minuted when the board was reconstituted at the meeting; the offer approved by a committee that the reorganization disbanded. What expires is the matter's place in the process, since the successor body starts it at zero. What is taken is a counterparty, the specific body whose yes was available. The clock is the ratifier's own calendar, election, session, or term. The move that would have kept it is the vote scheduled before adjournment, the carry-over motion, the approval minuted rather than agreed in the hallway. The treaty cases are simplified, since most unratified treaties were eventually refused by someone; the clean form is the legislative bill, which dies by the thousand each session with no recorded no. The wanting here has to be for the minute and not the nod, because the nod dies with the body that gave it. It adds to deal-deaths' Ratifier's other deal, where the ratifier wanted a different bargain, the ratifier that wanted this one and was gone before the vote. It is not Landlord changes, where the counterparty is replaced by transfer, since here it is replaced by the calendar.

Landlord changes: you want the promise to hold, and it was made to you by a person rather than written on the paper that transfers, so it dies at the counterparty's next transfer, which you do not control and often do not see. The renewal promised by the landlord who sells the building to a buyer not bound by unrecorded promises; the 'we'll take you back' from a manager who leaves; the side letter with a fund's partner that the fund's successor manager has never seen; the supplier's verbal priority that vanishes with the account executive. What is taken is a counterparty, the one whose word held the option. The clock is the register, the deed, the fund agreement, the offer letter on letterhead, on which the option was never written, so the successor takes free of it. The move that would have kept it is recording: a memorandum of option on the title, a side letter countersigned by the entity, the promise put on the paper that binds successors, which costs the awkwardness of asking a friendly counterparty to bind their unknown replacement. You have to want the thing more than you want to be gracious about it. It adds to term-sheet-powers' Successor in the chair, where the replacement exercises a term the friend would not have, the mirror case, where the replacement declines to honour a term the friend gave. It is not Chair grown over, where the counterparty stays and the shape goes.

Chair grown over: you want to come back, and the seat you would come back to is a vacancy the counterparty has not yet re-planned, so it is absorbed at the counterparty's next planning cycle without anyone declining your return. The leave taken with no return date whose post is redistributed among three people at the next reorganization; the budget line reallocated at year end; the supplier's line retooled for the customer who stayed; the co-founder's seat that the remaining founders stop leaving empty at the next hire. What expires is the return to the seat, since employment there afterwards is a new negotiation from the outside. What is taken is a capability on the counterparty's side, the shape that could receive you. The clock is the counterparty's planning cadence, quarterly, annual, the next reorganization, which sets the expiry without reference to you at all. The move that would have kept it is a dated return, a leave rather than a resignation, a reservation the cycle must respect, or the return itself before the cycle turns. Wanting to come back is not a reservation; only a date is. It adds to traces-of-the-unlived's Vacancy tenant, where preparation for a future breeds its opponents, the case in which no one opposes the return and the absence is simply absorbed. It is not forms-of-return's Reentry burn, a road open and hostile one way, since this road has closed.

Petition that goes stale: you want many yeses at once, and each yes rots while you are out collecting the next, so an option that needs simultaneous assent expires unless the gathering outruns the decay of every assent; a coordination has a half-life. The recall petition whose signatures older than sixty days are invalid under Michigan's rule, or must all fall within California's hundred and sixty days; the tender offer's minimum condition that must be met by the offer's expiry; the crowd in the square that goes home; the reunion that becomes impossible one death at a time. What is taken is a coordination. The clock is the validity window on each act of assent, written by the rule or by the assenter's own attention. The move that would have kept it is a gathering rate, paid circulators, a date agreed in advance, a pact that binds the early yeses until the last arrives. The recall and tender cases are observed and the crowd is analogy. The appetite has to be for all of it at once; a taste for one signature at a time is how the first ones spoil. It adds to who-can-be-bound's Place in line, an ordering lost by leaving, the coordination lost by others' leaving. It is not Session ends, where one body's calendar kills the matter, since here many small calendars do.

Outgrown the buyer: you wanted more and you got it, and the getting moved the buyer out of reach. The option to sell to the natural acquirer expires at the round that prices the company above what the acquirer can pay at all: a market capitalization smaller than the price, a wage cap, a fund's concentration limit, and past those a board's approval ceiling, with nobody at either table declining. The company whose preference stack now exceeds the largest deal its three strategic buyers have ever done; the player whose wage outgrows every club in the league but two; the practice too large for any partner to buy in and too small to be listed. What is taken is a counterparty, the buyer whose capacity was the option. The clock is the acquirer's capacity, readable in its market value and its deal history, set against your own price, which each round raises. The move that would have kept it is the sale at the last price under the ceiling, which was never seen as the last, or a round sized to stay under it, which is the one choice a founder is never advised to make. This is analytical, since every observed case can be read as a buyer that would have paid more, so the item stands as a mechanism and not a count. It is the one item on the map where the appetite eats its own exit: the price you drove up is the price nobody can pay. It adds to market-deaths' Slowed past the rot, where a market thins from the outside, the market for the holder that the holder thins by growing. It is not Chair grown over, where the counterparty re-plans, since here the counterparty is unchanged and the holder has left its range.

Pour the foundation: you want to keep a permission that a third party's rule change is about to take, and no paper will keep it; only an act in the world will. The building that may proceed under the old zoning only if the developer has substantially begun in reliance on a valid permit before the ordinance passes; the footings poured the week of the council vote; the nonconforming use that survives the new code only if it is in use on the effective date; the grandfathered rate kept only by the account that was open. What is taken is a permission. The clock is the code and the vested-rights doctrine, which in most states vests on construction begun and in a few, as in Washington, on a complete application, so the last act differs by jurisdiction and the holder who knows which has a different week. The move that would have kept it is the hole in the ground before the vote, an exercise begun rather than a filing made, so the option can be preserved only by starting to use it. The wanting here has to become concrete, literally: nothing short of the pour counts. It adds to first-mover-forecloses, which holds the rival who changes the rules on purpose, the rule that changes for reasons of its own. It is not Slot flown empty, where the exercise must be repeated to keep the right, since here one beginning vests it for good.

Slot flown empty: the permission expires by disuse and is kept only by exercise, so the clock runs while you do nothing and stops when you act, and the act that keeps it is the exercise emptied of everything you wanted it for. The airport slot that must be flown eighty percent of the season or returned, which had airlines flying empty aircraft in early 2020 until the rule was waived; the water right under prior appropriation forfeited after five years without beneficial use, which has fields irrigated in a drought to keep them; the trade mark abandoned after three years' non-use; the mining claim kept by annual labour; the department budget spent in the last quarter so that it is not cut. What is taken is a permission. The clock is the regulator's usage ledger. The move that keeps it is the empty flight, which costs the whole price of using the option and returns nothing but the option, so that keeping and using become the same act and the option's upkeep is its exercise price. You have to want the permission enough to consume it for nothing, over and over, and never be embarrassed by the empty seats. It adds to runway-illusions' Stamp's clock, whose licence lapses without hours logged and whose clock no cash extends, the price at which it can be extended after all, the hours flown for nobody. It adds to tollgates-that-must-buy's Stamp with an expiry, where the gate must spend its stamp, the permission-holder who must burn the permission to keep it, and to power-trades' Leased strike, where disuse makes a power unbelieved, the disuse that forfeits it by rule. It is not Pour the foundation, one act that vests, since here no act ever finishes the keeping.

Thawed to be ready: you wanted to be ready, and readiness started a decay the unready state did not have, so the option to wait expired because the option to act was made ready. The vaccine vial that keeps for months frozen, weeks once thawed, and hours once punctured; the epoxy whose pot life begins at mixing; the drawn dose; the armed fuze; the reagent brought to room temperature; the opened surgical field; the reserve army that cannot be held at the frontier through the harvest it was drawn from. What is taken is a capability, the good itself spoiling in its ready state. The clock is a chemistry, or a season, that begins at preparation. The move that would have kept it is not preparing, or preparing in the smallest unit, the single-dose vial, the small mix, the tranche thawed for the day's bookings, so the clinic that thaws a tray to be sure of serving whoever comes has bought readiness with the doses it will discard at closing. The appetite for readiness is real and it has a price, and the price is paid in the good itself. This is the mirror of Slot flown empty, where the option dies of not being touched, since here it dies of being touched, and a holder who holds both must burn the one and refrain from readying the other. It is not lead-time-floors' Understudy, a finished copy waiting, since the understudy does not spoil for having been rehearsed; and not Kept on the machine, where the harm falls on the holder and is billed by the day, since here it falls on the good.

First or never: you want to keep the objection, and you keep it only by taking it before any other move on a linked matter, so its clock is your own next act rather than a date; do nothing and you keep it, do anything adjacent and you lose it. The objection to the court's jurisdiction over the defendant that is waived if left out of the first response; the patent that is dead in Europe on the morning of the conference talk and a year later in the United States; the appeal waived by accepting the settlement; the election of remedies; the defect in the goods that must be objected to before the goods are used; the 'speak now' at the wedding. What is taken is a permission. The clock is a rule that binds the option to a position in a sequence, and the sequence is written in a different place than the option, in the rules of procedure, the patent statute, the sales code, so the holder learns the order from the loss. The move that would have kept it is the ordering itself: the provisional application filed the morning of the talk, the reservation written into the first filing, the objection lodged before the goods are unpacked, each of which costs nothing but the knowledge that an order exists. The wanting here is for sequence: you have to want the objection before you let yourself want anything else in the matter. It is not Slot flown empty, where the holder's inaction runs the clock, since here inaction is the only thing that keeps it; and not Bar date in the newspaper, since there is no date and the holder is the only one who can strike.

Rollback horizon: you want to be able to go back, and the way back closes at the first act the new state performs that the old state cannot read, so the window is the pause between the change and its first consequence, and it closes without anyone deciding to close it. The migration that can be rolled back until the new service writes its first record in a shape the old schema rejects; the merger reversible until the first combined payroll; the new address reversible until the first piece of mail arrives there; the reorganization reversible until the first hire is made into the new chart; the currency changeover until the first contract is written in the new unit. What is taken is a capability, the old state's ability to take over from here. The clock is the first write, which the new state performs in the ordinary course of doing what you wanted it for, and which is not a decision about the reversal at all. The move that would have kept it is the expand-and-contract shape, writing to both for a season so that the old can still read, at the price of running two and of a season in which neither is the truth. You cannot want the new state's first meal and the old state's way back at the same time without paying for both. It adds to pivot-invariants, which name the retained assets that make leaving cheap, the moment at which one of them is lost, and to undo-costs, which bills a reversal that remains possible, the reversal that stops being possible. It is not Thawed to be ready, where readiness spoils the good, since here the new state's use closes the way back to the old.

Kept on the machine: you want the bridge to hold until the far shore, and the bridge is what eats the shore. The option is held open by a device or an upkeep whose own running accumulates a harm or whose lapse is one-way, so the deadline is the machine's and not the situation's. The patient on ECMO as a bridge to transplant who becomes ineligible for the transplant the machine was keeping her alive for, since bleeding, infection, and clotting rise with each week on circuit and centres set a duration beyond which candidacy is reviewed; the mothballed mine kept dry by pumps whose stopping floods the workings past reopening; the ship in the reserve fleet whose hull is kept by cathodic protection that a budget line can end; the interim chief who has run the company past the point where the search can bring in an outsider. What is taken is a capability, the eligibility or the workings. The clock is the bridge itself, its complication rate or its upkeep bill. The move that would have kept it is a listing at the moment of cannulation, a search begun the day the interim was named, a decision to stop pumping taken while a sale was still possible, each of which treats the bridge's start as the option's deadline. The ECMO limits are centre practice and are simplified. The appetite that keeps the patient alive is the appetite that must also, on the same day, want the transplant list, or it has wanted only the bridge. It adds to lead-time-floors' Bridge, a degraded replacement priced by the hour, the bridge that ends the option it holds open. It is not Standstill with a term, where the clock is a date the counterparty signs, since here the clock is a harm nobody signs.

Standstill with a term: you wanted to keep the option open, so you bought a pause, and the pause is written on a paper with a date, so a situation that had no deadline now has one, and the paper's renewal belongs to the other side, who now knows exactly what the pause is worth to you. The tolling agreement that stops the limitations clock you could have stopped alone by filing and that expires in twelve months unless the adversary signs again; the negotiated leave of absence that dates a job which had no date and is extended only if the employer signs; the forbearance agreement that holds the lender's foreclosure for ninety days; the furlough whose recall rights run six months; the standstill in a takeover that keeps the bidder from buying shares and ends on the day it says. What is taken is a permission, the leave to remain in the paused state. The clock is the pause's own instrument, and its clock is the only clock in the situation that you wrote. The move that would have kept it is the renewal asked for before the counterparty learns it is needed, or a pause written without a term, which is rarely granted, since the Korean armistice is the exception that has no renewal date and is still called temporary. The statutory pauses, the twelve weeks of the family-leave statute and the restraining order's fourteen days, are the same date without the mechanism, since the term is a rule's and the renewal belongs to a court or to no one, so the holder gets the deadline without paying the counterparty for it; those are runway-illusions' Stamp's clock. Wanting the pause is what priced it, and the adversary read the price off your signature. It adds to impasse-inventions' cooling-off right, reversibility offered as a chip, the bill the chip carries. It is not lead-time-floors' No-shop, which serializes the search, since here the search is stopped and the stopping is what expires.
